instructions.text: Before any separately owner-controlled install update, identify files the owner added under references/archetypes/ and preserve them through the owner in .tackle/archetypes/ or ~/.tackle/archetypes/. The installed artifact is SKILL.md plus references/ plus scripts/. Migration never performs the update or moves/deletes owner additions itself; if preservation is unresolved, keep the install-related step pending.

If a retired loopback live producer is actually observed, have its owner stop it before a separately authorized install update. Current Tackle ships no live producer. Migration neither starts a replacement service nor stops arbitrary processes; absence of the producer creates no action.

Use current installed scripts and their documented direct procedures, not saved historical recipe programs or a replacement task runner. An explicit request authorizes only its documented script use; ordinary project commands remain available under their own scope. Current lint uses installed lint.py and canonical rows, citation grounding retains its two phases, and scaffold/evaluation use the current installed guides. Migration performs no installation or network operation.

The old no-helper/two-part install instruction is superseded by the current three-part artifact SKILL.md, references/ and scripts/. Observe installed resources and manifest before proceeding. Do not delete tracked project helpers or fixtures as a migration step. Only the owner-controlled update procedure may remove its exact verified legacy tombstone tackle-check, preserving tackle and unrelated sentinels; migration neither updates nor deletes install content.

Preserve the project boundary that docs/plans/ and docs/seeds/ are both gitignored and neither ships in the install artifact. Check the observed project policy without changing the original or neighboring files. A missing required boundary needs an owner decision in its own allowed scope, not silent staging, publication or a project-wide edit by migration.

Do not execute historical blanket deletion of todo.md, tasks.md, checklist.md or execution-strategy.md. Preserve historical-only files and record their mapping or historical role; use only supported structural adapters for actual current renames. Keep one current task-board state and resolve dependencies from the current plan/board contract rather than maintaining a pasted second graph. Any proposed removal outside the compiled structural map needs separate owner authority.

Historical automatic/daily self-update and old update-command instructions are superseded. Ordinary invocation and migration perform no network access or installation mutation. Only the owner-controlled out-of-band update workflow verifies and replaces the three-part artifact; installing/updating never selects or migrates a workspace. An already-current artifact requires no install action.

exceptions: Already-current installation produces no install action; owner-controlled update and removal boundaries apply.

Preserve exact checks, test/replay inputs, correction lineage and historical completed/blocked/skipped/interrupted states; unavailable evidence stays unavailable. Started/Checking/Interrupted tasks retain their procedure/counters until their deliberate boundary.

A legacy row without an exact run_id remains legacy-scoped. Copy and hash these bytes before transformation; never rewrite, backfill, re-grade or reorder them, and leave the original and neighbors unchanged.

instructions.text: For every Complete task on the board, hash its brief with `sha256sum <brief>`, or `shasum -a 256 <brief>` without `sha256sum`. Retain the exact baseline and original brief bytes before any other edit to a closed brief. A conflicting existing baseline holds; never recompute it to match an edited brief.

Put `**Brief sha256**: <64 lowercase hex digits>` on its own line in the task's report, outside code fences. Place it right before the report's `Final status:` line, or right before its `**Remains**:` line when it has none. Then append `Brief sha256 T-NN: <the same hash>` on its own line, outside code fences, to the end of `history.md`. History only grows: never edit an older entry. That report line and the history line are the only changes adoption makes to a closed task's records. Do both before any other edit to a closed brief. Skipped and Unverifiable reports may carry both too. Preserve an existing identical receipt; a conflicting value is pending, not overwritten.

After recording the baseline, a closed brief changes only by erratum. An active decision authorizes the edit; then append `**Brief erratum**: D-NN · sha256 <hash after the edit>` to its report. Retain the pre-edit baseline and decision; no generic repair or silent closed-history edit is allowed.

End every required Complete report with `**Remains**: none`, or `**Remains**:` followed by the actual O-NN obligation IDs left behind. Resolve unknown Remains from the actual report/owner; never infer none from a terminal board mark, an empty list or a reviewer label. Add only a specifically required missing adoption receipt, preserving existing closed bytes and blocking conflicting values.

On selected open work use the task-board template’s obligations section: every obligation outliving its task has an O-NN row with owner, trigger, state Open and discharge check. Append a new history State snapshot naming every Open ID in Active obligations; never edit an older snapshot. Preserve obligations through task split/merge/rename and require actual discharge evidence.

Future closures require the actual report and Coordinator/independent checker evidence under the current RUN protocol before the board becomes Complete. A stub or a named reviewer alone is not current proof. Preserve existing closed reports, legacy sign-offs and the original state without retrospective repair or regrading; current-work/handoff are projections, never canonical state. Missing current required evidence holds its owning open-work closure.

exceptions: Conflicting existing receipt or baseline values block; no generic historical repair.

Use `full` for the [next wave](verify.md#milestone-readiness) and for any brief whose row is Ready to run, In progress or Checking. Use `interface` for the rest. Row 18 fails a Ready to run row that names an interface brief. Edit the brief of an In progress or Checking task only at that task's boundary, never during an attempt.

Give a brief raised to full the symbol ledger of task.tmpl.md. Under Interface and invariants, `**Produces**` and `**Consumes**` each hold `none` or indented sub-items. Every consumed name gets one source: `from T-NN`, `from T-NN [sibling]` or `exists` with an anchored citation. A `from T-NN` task must be an ancestor through `Depends on`. A `[sibling]` source must also appear in the brief's own `Depends on` cell. A name has one producing brief; row 18 fails a name that two briefs produce. The task-boundary rule applies here too. An interface brief needs no ledger.

The owner's brief must cite the decision id and, at `full` detail, carry each named clause compiled. When a decision with these lines supersedes an earlier one, the earlier heading names it, as `⤴ superseded by D-NN`. Row 19 fails a heading that names another, and a still-active predecessor is no finding.
